headline: US stocks recover from a deep sell-off, but technology still lags
summary: The S&P 500 closed down 0.25% at 7,182.78 after trading down more than 3% in the morning. The Nasdaq Composite finished 0.62% lower, while the Dow gained 0.33% and the Russell 2000 rose 0.71%. Seven of 11 sectors advanced. The equal-weight S&P 500 ETF gained 0.83% while SPY lost 0.29%, suggesting the recovery reached beyond the largest companies. Materials, industrials and financials finished higher, while technology and consumer discretionary lagged. The index close was flat enough to obscure how sharply both the level and the leadership changed during the session.

highlights.title: A broader recovery than the index close suggests
highlights.text: Small caps and the equal-weight index recovered more strongly than the Nasdaq. That fits a rotation away from some large technology names, but the day’s prices cannot show who sold or why. Dell and Workday recovered from earlier weakness while several large cloud names still fell. If that split persists after the holiday, it would be stronger evidence of changing leadership than a single afternoon rebound.

highlights.title: Lower Treasury yields helped, but did not settle credit concerns
highlights.text: The ten-year yield fell despite firm inflation and growth readings cited in the report. That makes a simple story about rising long-term rates a poor fit for the sell-off. Broad investment-grade and high-yield bond ETFs rose 0.48% and 0.12%, respectively. The report also cited wider default-protection spreads for several AI issuers. Those signals can coexist: falling Treasury yields can lift bond ETFs even as investors demand more protection on specific borrowers.

highlights.title: What would change the view
highlights.text: Friday’s shortened US session is the first test, but thinner holiday trading can exaggerate price moves. Look for the breadth improvement to carry into Monday: continued strength in equal-weight and small-cap stocks, alongside stabilising technology shares, would support the rotation view. If breadth rolls over and broad high-yield credit weakens too, the risk would look less confined to large technology borrowers.

highlights.title: Market sentiment: near-term hedges stayed expensive
highlights.text: The report put nine-day implied volatility near 29.61, above spot VIX at about 28.3 and the three-month reading at 26.29. The premium for near-term protection persisted despite the afternoon rebound. Commentary about institutional hedging is useful context, but the brief has no fresh positioning tally or retail survey for the session. Neither public commentary nor trading volume establishes who bought the dip.

forecast.outlook: Upside and downside have equal weight
forecast.horizon: 27 November–1 December US sessions · S&P 500 final close
forecast.method: Original section 6.2 forecast; issue time uses the verified AM report generation timestamp in all three reported time zones. Three-method average; the report uses published five-point probabilities. Base includes both endpoints.
forecast.watch_next: Watch whether broader participation holds through the shortened Friday session and into Monday.

limitations: Reported Treasury and volatility readings vary by source or snapshot time. Issuer-level credit observations are not a measure of whole-market credit conditions. The 18 scored windows in the source ledger do not establish calibration.
